Software / System LibRaw — src/decoders/pana8.cpp
Versions Affected Prior to commit 777f20ae21c611a78021bd051fbbf1e71eae78f2
Language / Platform Python PoC (RW2 file mutator)
Authentication Required No (local file processing)
Network Access Required No

Summary

LibRaw’s GetDBit() function, used when decoding Panasonic RW2 raw image files, can return the value 17 when no Huffman table match is found. However, the huff_coeff[] array is declared with only 17 elements (valid indices 0-16), so this out-of-bounds return value causes huff_coeff[17] to be accessed — undefined behavior confirmed via UBSan and AddressSanitizer. Applications processing untrusted RW2 files (image editors, photo managers using LibRaw) could crash or leak process memory.

item.title: Ollama GGUF Heap Out-of-Bounds Read During Quantization — CVE-2026-7482
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value
Date Added 2026-07-05
Last Updated 2026-05
Author / Researcher szybnev
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-7482
Category misc
Severity Medium
CVSS Score Not specified in source
Status PoC
Tags ollama, gguf, heap-overflow, out-of-bounds-read, quantization, llm-serving, docker
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Ollama (GGUF model loader / quantization pipeline)
Versions Affected Ollama < 0.17.1 (reproduced against 0.17.0; fixed in 0.17.1)
Language / Platform Python 3 (exploit/reproduction script), targeting Ollama’s Go-based server via its HTTP API
Authentication Required No (local Ollama API, no auth by default)
Network Access Required Yes — local/lab Ollama API access; also requires local Docker access to the vulnerable container to extract generated artifacts

Summary

Ollama versions prior to 0.17.1 do not validate that a GGUF model file’s declared tensor size matches the actual bytes present in the file. By crafting a GGUF file whose tensor metadata declares a much larger shape than the data actually written, and then triggering quantization of that model via Ollama’s /api/create endpoint, the quantization code reads past the end of the truncated buffer (a heap out-of-bounds read) and incorporates the out-of-bounds bytes into the generated quantized model artifact. The author reliably reproduced the OOB condition and confirmed (via differential comparison against a zero-filled control file) that out-of-bounds bytes influence the output, but was explicitly unable to demonstrate reliable recovery of plaintext secrets or canary strings from the resulting artifact in black-box testing — the author is candid that this is a narrower result than a full data-disclosure exploit.

Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System rldns 1.3 (open-source DNS server)
Versions Affected 1.3 (fixed in 1.4)
Language / Platform C (exploit); target runs on Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, x86_64
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

rldns is an open-source DNS server for Linux, FreeBSD, and NetBSD. Version 1.3 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read that can be triggered remotely by sending a specially crafted, malformed DNS-like UDP packet, causing the server process to crash and resulting in denial of service. The included PoC is a small C program that builds a fixed 16-byte malformed packet and sends it via a raw UDP socket to the target’s DNS port. Version 1.4 of rldns contains the fix for this issue.
